problem: Prior object-relation modeling for VLN uses shallow GCNs (over-smoothing) or external knowledge (ConceptNet, LLMs, image-text datasets) that has a gap with the navigation environment. Adding relation modeling also makes agents revisit locations, lengthening paths.
motivation: Object relations can improve grounding and navigation, but relations must reflect the real environment and temporal continuity of the trajectory. Detailed relation tracking caused redundant revisits that hurt SPL, so efficiency needs explicit handling.
key_idea: Learn object relations from within the environment along two axes, temporal (cross-attention between observed objects and instruction nouns) and spatial (a distance-based co-occurrence matrix over all viewpoints), and add a Turning Back Penalty loss to discourage revisits.
insight: Both relation modules raise success rates (OSR/SR/RGS) but also lengthen trajectories, so SPL barely improves (Table 4); adding the TBP loss cuts TL (23.52 to 22.00 on REVERIE val unseen) and lifts SPL (34.56 to 36.79). TOR helps more than SOR, attributed to small training sets, and combining both is best. Penalizing revisits at inference hurts SR (Table 6) because it blocks error correction, so the penalty works only as a training loss.
method: Object noun features: build a noun database from Matterport3D object labels, select matching instruction words, add position/type embeddings and encode with a transformer to get noun representations.
Temporal Object Relations (TOR): cross-attention with object features as query and noun features as key gives T = FC(O_t)·W^; M_t = T·W^, recomputed at each node along the trajectory.

Spatial Object Relations (SOR): a global matrix E is accumulated over all viewpoints, adding k1/(k2·||view diff|| + k3·||depth diff||) for co-visible object pairs; the sub-matrix E' for current objects and instruction nouns gives N_t = E'·W^.
Feature fusion: Q_t = a1·O_t + a2·M_t + a3·N_t with learnable weights summing to 1 (init 0.8/0.1/0.1), concatenated with panoramic image features R_t and fed to the DUET dual-scale graph transformer.

Turning Back Penalty (TBP): L_TBP = sum_i softmax(p)_i · d_i, where d_i is the cumulative length of repeatedly traversed path when moving to candidate b_i, so probability mass on revisiting moves is penalized.

Training: DUET-style pretraining (MLM, MRC, SAP, OG), then fine-tuning with L = L_SAP + L_OG + 0.2·L_TBP under a pseudo-interactive demonstrator. R2R uses TOR only, with panoramic features standing in for objects.

setting.backbone: DUET dual-scale graph transformer (LXMERT-initialized) with TOR/SOR modules, trained
setting.training_data: REVERIE original + DUET-synthesized augmented data; SOON original data with cleaned boxes; R2R with PREVALENT augmented R2R data; pretraining 100k/40k/200k iterations on REVERIE/SOON/R2R
setting.observation: panoramic RGB with object features (annotated boxes for REVERIE, BUTD detections for SOON, ViT-B/16 features), topological map, instruction
setting.privileged: none at inference beyond dataset-provided object boxes (REVERIE); SOR matrix built from training-environment observations

results: On REVERIE test-unseen the method reaches SR 55.31 and SPL 40.37, beating the DUET baseline (50.67/36.27) and GridMM (53.13/36.60). On SOON test-unseen it obtains SR 37.09, SPL 23.60 versus GridMM 36.27/21.25. On R2R gains are small (val-unseen SR 71/SPL 61 vs baseline 71/60), with larger gains on val seen.
limitations: Relations may be inaccurate because training datasets are small; SOR gives smaller gains than TOR, and R2R lacks object annotations so SOR cannot be used and gains are marginal.
The SOR matrix relies on the training environments' object annotations and depth/view constants (k1,k2,k3) that are hand-set.
Evaluation is limited to simulator benchmarks with no real-robot tests; some baselines are compared with replicated DUET results.
